rationale: C21 is explicitly identified by the child as the April 8 letter being answered and supplies the child's central drafting framework. Both letters enumerate the same disarmament measures—supervised limits on fissionable material, reductions of existing weapons stocks through peaceful transfers, suspension of testing, Open Skies, and peaceful use of outer space—and then argue for immediate technical studies of verification and control before final political agreement. The child materially reuses both C21's language and its proposal-to-technical-studies sequence. C23 contains an earlier version of much of this machinery, while C08 closely parallels several substantive proposals but less fully matches the child's structure.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In my letter of April eighth, I again proposed an internationally supervised cutoff of the use of new fissionable materials for weapons purposes and the reduction of existing weapons stocks by transfer to peaceful purposes; an agreed limitation or suspension of testing; "open skies," and the international use of outer space for peaceful purposes.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It refuses to agree to an internationally supervised cut-off of the use of new fissionable material for weapons purposes and the reduction of existing weapons stocks by transfers to peaceful purposes. ... You will recall, Mr. Chairman, my "Open Skies" proposal ... You will also recall my proposals for the international use of outer space for peaceful purposes.
shared_material.explanation: The child expressly reprises C21's distinctive bundle of disarmament proposals, with closely shared wording.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I proposed that we start our technical people to work immediately upon the practical problems involved. These studies were called for by the United Nations General Assembly.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Why should we not at once put our technicians to work to study together and advise as to what specific control measures are necessary...? The United Nations General Assembly has called for technical disarmament studies.
shared_material.explanation: This is a concrete reuse of C21's immediate-technician-study proposal and its supporting appeal to the General Assembly.

shared_material.child_excerpt: They would include the practical problems of supervision and control which, you and I agree, are in any event indispensable to dependable disarmament agreements.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The United States is also prepared ... to work with the Soviet Union ... on the technical problems involved in international controls. We both recognize that international control would be necessary.
shared_material.explanation: Both texts use the same administrative mechanism: joint technical work on indispensable international verification and control.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The completion of such technical studies in advance of a political agreement would obviate a considerable period of delay and uncertainty.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: If there is ever to be an agreed limitation or suspension of testing ... plans for international control should be in instant readiness.
shared_material.explanation: The child develops C21's sequencing rationale that technical control plans should be completed before the ultimate political agreement.
